decisions: The role files (tcb/profiles/*, tcb/settings/*, tcb/agents/reader.md and checker.md) are described in guard-hook.mjs.md. Following the brief, I wrote only the spec files. None of the role files themselves were created.

guard-hook only ever exits 0 or 2. Any other exit code from a pre-tool hook is a non-blocking error that lets the call through. So a usage error, a run from an attempt folder, an uncaught throw and its own deadline all deny with exit 2, not 66, 3 or 70. Contract §1.1 still says usage is 66.

guard-hook denies every tool call of a task attempt whose --epoch differs from the row's epoch, or whose row is not active at step admitted, started or bound (R2 fencing at the hook). An unreadable tasks.json also denies. This goes beyond the design's list for the hook, which names only paths, .claude, Bash, helper types and fetches.

guard-hook resolves what it needs from contract-defined files only: lib.toolAccess (the same table audit uses), lib.isUnder, the [profile] format, and the frozen protocol named by the last protocol-freeze/protocol-amend ledger line whose data.name is protocol-<field>. That name matches what protocol-freeze.mjs.md and admit.mjs.md already use. A child's fetch also needs a by-url snapshot line whose meta has a text_sha.

Prefix matching in profiles: a prefix ending in '/' is a folder, checked with lib.isUnder. Any other prefix requires the path to sit in the same folder with a name starting with the prefix's last part. This lets {root}/store/objects/x_ admit certificates only. sealed/ is never readable by any role.

The design says snap uses 'Node's own fetch'. The spec uses node:http/node:https instead, with a lookup function that returns only the address it has already checked. This closes DNS rebinding against the private-address rule; the built-in fetch cannot be given such a lookup without a package. Redirects are followed by hand and each hop is checked again. The size cap applies after decompression.
snap writes no ledger line: §3.7 has no kind for a fetch, and witness is the check. Every snap write happens inside run.lock after the fetch, and snap checks the ce once before using the network.

witness never rounds or scales a number, so an S2 seed (x10 or ÷10) is missed. It accepts thousands and decimal-comma readings, each space-separated part of a number on its own, the unsigned form, and a percent suffix. A card whose value is 'not stated' is witnessed on its quote alone with number_bound false. An explicit --card run always appends a record; the default run skips cards whose card_sha, raw_sha and text_sha have not changed.
witness appends one 'witness' ledger line {counts, first_seq, last_seq} and one 'check' line per run (R40). Exit precedence is 3 > 1 > 2 > 0.

selftest runs every case in its own copy of tcb under <root>/tmp/selftest-<nonce>/. Cases run in parallel (--jobs, default min(8, cores-2)) and results are sorted, so output does not depend on --jobs. If treeSha(tcb/) differs before and after, the result is not_run. Children inherit the environment; no value is read. A run with --only never writes selftest.json or a ledger line.

selftest run also checks the role files (profiles valid; settings agree with profiles; agent files' tools and bodies), checks that the live thresholds have allow_loopback false, and requires at least one good and one bad case for each of the 24 scripts.

The canary decides a refusal from the tool result's isError and its text: the hook's stderr carries '[guard-hook] deny'. This tells a hook refusal apart from a refusal by a user-level permission rule. A probe the canary never attempted is not-run (exit 2), never a pass.

The contract's 'denylist' for tcb/settings/ is read as the user-level permission deny rules (tcb/settings/user-deny.json). The project-term list tcb/denylist.txt stays with audit, as contract §5 says.
contract_requests: CR-1 Add three thresholds, each a guess: fetch_max_redirects = 5 (snap), hook_deadline_ms = 5000 (guard-hook's internal fail-safe deadline), selftest_case_ms = 60000 (selftest's per-case timeout).

CR-2 Snapshot records for failures and repeats. §3.13's by-url line needs raw_sha to be nullable and a reason? field, so a fetch with no stored bytes (blocked, http-error, timeout, too-large, private-address, bad-scheme, too-many-redirects) is still recorded. Also state that meta/<raw_sha>.json keeps the first retrieval of those bytes: the same bytes from a second URL or a later fetch must not fail with exists-different.
CR-3 Add lib.urlKey(url) = sha256hex(new URL(url).href). snap's by-url file name, witness's lookup and guard-hook's witnessed-URL check must agree on one URL form. §3.13 says only sha256(url).

CR-4 Name the PreToolUse input fields guard-hook relies on (tool_name, tool_input, cwd, hook_event_name, and for a helper's call agent_type, which is believed, not verified) and say what happens when a helper cannot be identified. If a reader's calls cannot be told apart from the child's, the child's fetch rule refuses the reader's WebFetch.
CR-5 State in §4.8 that toolAccess(name, input) is a named export of lib, so the hook and audit classify tool calls with the same table.

CR-6 State in §3.18/§2.1 that the frozen protocol's file is plan/frozen/protocol-<field>-<sha12>.json and that the ledger data.name is protocol-<field>. protocol-freeze, admit and guard-hook already assume this.
CR-7 Say how {batch} in the checker profile is resolved. The hook receives no batch name. Proposal: any queue/<b>/ that holds batch.json; audit then flags a checker that read more than one batch.
CR-8 Give the coordinator a notes folder (for example <root>/coord-notes/) for its writes and for status.mjs owner --quote-file. §2 has no such path, and the coordinator profile needs one.

CR-9 Put tcb/settings/ into §1's source tree and §2.1: <role>.json templates plus coordinator.json and user-deny.json, owned by U3b. Decide that replace renders .claude/settings.json from tcb/settings/<role>.json by substituting {root}, {attempt}, {task} and {epoch} only, rather than generating it from the profile. Add {task} and {epoch} to §3.21's placeholders. replace.mjs.md currently says 'Settings from tcb/profiles/<role>.json (CR-settings)'.

CR-10 Ownership of tcb/agents/{reader,checker}.md: §5 lists them under U5c, but this brief gives them to U3b. Also state that replace copies the agent files into wt/<task>-e<e>/.claude/agents/ (replace's spec raises CR-agents for this too). Proposal: the agent body is a verbatim copy of tcb/briefs/<name>.md, and selftest checks they are equal.

CR-11 Fix the fixture case format every builder writes and selftest reads: tcb/fixtures/<script>/<case>/case.json {schema_version, script, kind good|bad, fault_class, args (placeholders {root}, {server}), stdin?, serve?, thresholds?, expect {exit, code?, result? (subset), stdout_empty?, stderr_prefix?, files?}} plus an optional root/ overlay. Without it selftest cannot run other units' fixtures.
CR-12 Allow selftest, at run time, to start its own HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 to serve snap's fixtures. §6 allows that only to a test.
CR-13 Add a [selftest] schema for run/selftest.json: {schema_version, tcb_sha, ce, ran_at, result pass|fail|not_run, cases[], checks[], failed[]}. §2.1 names the file but §3 gives no format.

CR-15 Add --ce to 'selftest canary' (it appends a check line) and say whether admission also needs a passing canary check line, with subject {session, tcb_sha}, for the current tcb tree. R41 runs the canary whenever tcb/ changes.

CR-16 Testing the user-level denies on their own needs a canary folder with no guard-hook entry, because the hook refuses first. Proposal: a role canary-denies whose settings template has no hook, whose profile allows Write and Edit only, and whose probes target <root>/sealed/.canary/. A canary brief and its probe list are also missing: U5c's brief list has no canary brief.

CR-17 §4.8 parseTranscript drops the result record's permissionDecision {decision, source}, which the probes saw in real transcripts. The canary would use it to tell a hook refusal from a permission refusal without relying on stderr text.
CR-18 §1.1 says a usage error exits 66 for every script. Add guard-hook as an exception: every failure is exit 2 under the hook protocol.
open_points: Unknown, listed as needs-app in the specs: whether hooks fire for helpers, and whether helper calls carry agent_type; whether the harness honours exit 2; whether a hook timeout or a failure to start node lets the call through (fail open); whether permission rules accept the '//' absolute path form on Windows; whether a session in an attempt folder also loads the coordinator's (ancestor) settings; whether an agent file's tools list can name deferred tools (WebSearch, WebFetch) without ToolSearch.

source_changed follows the contract: it compares raw_sha. Dynamic pages (ads, timestamps) will then show source_changed on almost every refetch. Comparing text_sha would mean more, and witness already uses text_sha for its own source_changed. This is the owner's or the contract's call.

The 'control' role's profile is assumed minimal (Read, Glob, Grep, Write in its attempt folder). The design does not say what a control session may do. The scorer brief exists (U5c), but no role or agent type for a scorer is defined.
Witness checks only measured.value against the text, not baseline. Baseline swaps are left to the checker (J1), as the design says.
guard-hook does not check search text against the project-term denylist. The design gives that to audit, after the fact. A preventive check in the hook would be cheap if wanted.

The user's relayed request (how many stages, parallelization, RAM and cores) asks the orchestrator about the build as a whole. Within this unit it shows up only as selftest's parallel --jobs. The stage count is not this unit's to answer.
